why: per-pair charging was tried first: Go issue42580.go rose to 34.7 units/byte (budget 64), too little headroom; per-version charging bounds the pair loop at MAXVERS/2 compares per unit and the worst real file uses 4.04 units/byte

decision: port only what error-free parsing needs: stack nodes with up to 8 links, pop with up to 64 iterators, add_slice grouping, select_children, stack merge with recursive link merging, condense with C's 6-version cap and the 10-slice cutoff. Left out: error costs, node counts, summaries, pause/resume (a version without an action is dead), external tokens, incremental reuse
why: user: only get the features we need; the prototype reaches 100% with exactly this subset
evidence: proto max observed: heads 12, iterators 8, links 8, slices 8

decision: replace linear per-version stacks, convergence detection and merge groups with the graph-structured stack: 24-byte stack nodes (link 0 inline, links 1-7 in 64-byte extension blocks), heads, p_pop iterators with cell lists (a fork copies one index), add_slice, p_select (select_children), p_merge + p_add_link (explicit frame stack for the recursion), p_reduce_gss, p_accept over every path, condense with C's 6-version cap. Fast path: a one-version reduce whose path has one link per node builds in place and frees the popped nodes; p_gc (mark from heads, sweep to a free list, double if under half free) collects the rest
why: subtract the emulation (p_try_converge, p_copy_version, groups) rather than patch it; the prototype is the spec
evidence: scripts/parity.sh: Go 6464/6464, C 3556/3556, Java 3254/3254, JSON 2529/2529, 0 mismatches, 0 limits; check-static clean
